title: GPU reservation bounce investigation journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal log while debugging recurrent capacity thrash observed on Dedicated GPU pools. Symptoms: repeated deallocation/reauthorization of reserved instances (~2–5 minute cycles) after canary rollout on 2026-01-28. Side-effect: long cold-to-warm tail, request queuing, and increased token cost from repeated warmups.

High-level hypothesis: a race between the pool reservation reconciler and the autoscaler scale-down policy when warmup probes spike latency during canary. Possible contributing factors: node labels mismatch, eviction scoring uses stale metrics, and prefix cache warm-start delays.

Timeline + quick notes:
- 2026-01-28 03:11 UTC: first alert - Dedicated pool-d-42 latency SLO breach, controller logs show rapid "reservation deleted" events.
- 2026-01-28 03:12 UTC: k8s events: kube-scheduler preempt attempted, then failed; pods rescheduled to new nodes.
- 2026-01-28 03:14 UTC: autoscaler decreased target from 10->5; immediate spike of pending requests; warmup tasks flood pool; re-add triggered to 12.
- 2026-01-28 03:18 UTC: rollback of canary; thrash stops for ~27 minutes, then returns during next traffic spike.

Commands I ran (copied outputs truncated):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-dedicated -o wide --show-labels | grep pool-d-42
  > pod/gpu-warm-1 READY 1/1 STATUS Running NODE gpu-node-1 labels: pool=pool-d-42,reserved=true

- kubectl describe pod gpu-warm-1 -n redwood-dedicated
  > Events:
    Normal Scheduled  2m  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned redwood-dedicated/gpu-warm-1 to gpu-node-1
    Warning Evicted  1m  kubelet  'eviction threshold reached' (score: 0.91)

- kc logs deployment/warmer -n redwood-dedicated --since=15m | tail -n 40
  > 2026-01-28T03:13:21Z WARN warmup: kvcache miss for model-a prefix; latency=784ms
  > 2026-01-28T03:13:21Z ERROR scheduler: reservation delete request received for reservation-id=res-117

- curl -sS 'https://metrics.redwood.ai/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(gpu_util[5m])' | jq .
  > returned spikes from 12% -> 94% for short bursts correlated with warmup requests

Logs snippets (important lines):
- controller: "Reservation(res-117) marked terminating, reason=scale-down-policy, owner=autoscaler"
- autoscaler: "requesting scale delta -5 from pool-d-42, based_on=99thpct_latency, lookback=2m"
- reconciler: "cannot bind reservation res-117 -> node gpu-node-3: label mismatch (reserved=true expected)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler uses latency spike signal from warmup probes (false positive) and issues scale-downs during transient warmup storms. This triggers reservation deletions which then cause the reconciler to attempt rebinds; repeated failures create bounce.
2) Reconciler node selection logic is brittle when nodes have stale labels from prior evictions (reserved label not applied fast enough). Race causes Reservation controller to delete and then re-create bindings.
3) Warmup workloads generate sudden KV cache misses that temporarily saturate CUDA init path; autoscaler sees infra-level latency and interprets as reduced capacity (inverted).
4) Canary rollout introduced an image that changes pod terminationGracePeriod resulting in faster node reclamation and more eviction-induced label churn.

What I tried (and results):
- Temporarily disabled scale-down for pool-d-42 (patch to autoscaler .spec.minReplicas=5) -> reduced bounce but cost increased; warmup still triggered localized evictions.
- Force-applied node label pipeline to ensure 'reserved=true' is present before binding; observed one successful bind but then kubelet eviction removed pod due to memory pressure.
- Increased warmup concurrency limit in warmer to 4->2 (throttle) -> better smoothing; latency spike amplitude reduced.
- Added a reconciliation delay of 45s before Reservation controller acts on a deletion event (testing in staging) -> seemed to reduce thrash frequency.

Next experiments to run (ordered):
- Add small hysteresis in autoscaler on latency metric: require sustained 90th pct for 3m before scale-down. (PR ready: infra#842)
- Capture kubelet eviction scoring metric during warmup; add debug trace to node exporter for evict_score.
- Deploy a pod disruption budget on warmer pods to avoid aggressive eviction during warmups.
- Run synthetic warmup replay at 0.5x, 1x, 2x to measure autoscaler sensitivity curve; capture CPU/GPU/kubelet metrics.
- Temporarily route canary traffic to Dedicated-other pool to see whether image change is causal.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Does the autoscaler read kubelet eviction_score or some custom node metric? (Jonas thinks eviction_score is surfaced via node-exporter metric 'node_kubelet_eviction_score')
- Would adding a short "reservation tombstone" window (60s) prevent deletion-reauthorization cycles?
- Are there version skew issues between the reservation controller and the node labeler sidecar?

Quick TODO (actions for me):
- [ ] Pull kubelet logs for gpu-node-1/2/3 from 2026-01-28 03:00-04:00 (SRE ticket if needed)
- [ ] Open canary routing test (add flag to traffic-router) and run with warmup replay
- [ ] Add autoscaler hysteresis experiment in staging and run overnight
- [ ] Draft short runbook blurb for P0: "If pool thrashing observed, increase minReplicas and throttle warmup"

Notes to self: keep this file terse. Link any long outputs to GCS blob and reference here. If we get a repro with logs, convert to writeup for infra postmortem.

Relevant snippets saved to GCS:
- gs://redwood-debug/inf-4178/kubelet-gpu-node-1-20260128.log
- gs://redwood-debug/inf-4178/warmer-logs-20260128.tgz

End of entry (2026-02-20).
